text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementAstronomyWas This the Exact Date of Van Gogh’s “Starry Night”?Astronomers look beyond the stars in search of Van Gogh’s inspirationJCBy Jake Currie1:15 PM CDT on October 23, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleWhile Starry Night is the traditional shorthand for Vincent van Gogh’s most famous work, its actual title is The Starry Night. It’s a more fitting name for such an iconic work, but does the painting depict an actual starry night, or did it spring from van Gogh’s vivid imagination? Powered By 10 ShareNextStayArt historians have debated the question for decades, but now astronomers are getting in on the action with a new study published in Scientific Reports. By taking a multidisciplinary approach that involves observational geometry, historical weather records, and even cicadas, they think they’ve nailed down the actual date of The Starry Night in question.Read more: “This Image from the Dark Energy Camera Is a Bit Van Gogh, No?”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
